title: Uncovering Audio-Text Alignment in Large Audio-Language Models through Cross-Modal Concept Neurons
abstract: arXiv:2610.28189v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While the language model backbone is pretrained on text alone, large audio-language models (LALMs) can, to a great extent, recognize acoustic attributes, such as emotion, speaker gender, and spoken language. However, it is unclear how the audio representation is integrated, if at all, with the other text representation before the model produces text. We hypothesize that there is a shared subspace where the audio and text representations are aligned. To test this hypothesis, we identify cross-modal neurons that are responsible for representing both audio and text. We find alignment between audio and text neurons to various degrees across three LALMs and four acoustic attribute types. Causal interventions, steering and deactivating the neurons, confirm that the cross-modal neurons are not just necessary for prediction but can also be manipulated.

translated_title: 通过跨模态概念神经元揭示大型音频-语言模型中的音频-文本对齐
translated_abstract: 尽管语言模型主干仅在文本上进行预训练，但大型音频-语言模型（LALMs）在很大程度上能够识别声学属性，例如情感、说话者性别和口语语言。然而，音频表示是否以及如何与文本表示整合，目前尚不清楚。我们假设存在一个共享子空间，音频和文本表示在其中是对齐的。为了验证这一假设，我们识别出负责同时表示音频和文本的跨模态神经元。我们在三个大型音频-语言模型和四种声学属性类型中发现音频神经元与文本神经元之间存在不同程度的对齐。因果干预实验——包括引导和关闭这些神经元——证实了跨模态神经元不仅对预测是必需的，而且还可以被操控。
tldr: 该研究发现了大型音频-语言模型中同时表示音频和文本的跨模态概念神经元，证实音频与文本表示在共享子空间中存在对齐，且这些神经元可通过因果干预被操控。
en_tdlr: The study identifies cross-modal concept neurons in large audio-language models that represent both audio and text, revealing audio-text alignment in a shared subspace that can be causally steered and deactivated.
